workflowIntro.title: Configure and run a benchmark
workflowIntro.content: The workflow page is the main benchmarking surface: follow ① name → ② pick models → ③ pick a quick template (optional) → ④ configure tasks. The bottom bar summarises task count, model count and estimated cost; hit Start Workflow to run it.

nav.title: Navigation
nav.content: Two groups: Benchmark runs tests and manages assets — Workflow, History, Template Library, Model Library, Model Identity. Tools holds Arena for quick single-model debugging, or head-to-head model duels.

stages.title: Three steps only
stages.content: Configure → run → results. This progress bar follows your current state so you always know where you are.

config.title: Set up the test
config.content: The left rail is numbered: ① name the workflow ② tick the models to compare ③ load a quick template to fill everything in (optional). The right side configures tasks: prompt, concurrency, iterations and more.

start.title: Run it
start.content: The sticky bottom bar summarises tasks, models, estimated requests and cost. When it looks right, click Start Workflow to execute every task in order. You can browse other pages while it runs — progress stays in sync.

identityIntro.title: Check what is really behind an endpoint
identityIntro.content: Relays sometimes serve a cheaper model than the one you asked for. These probes fingerprint the endpoint instead of trusting its label.

identityTarget.title: 1 · Choose what to test
identityTarget.content: Pick the provider and model you want to check. This is the endpoint you suspect, not the one you trust.

identityBaseline.title: 2 · Capture a baseline
identityBaseline.content: Select a trusted endpoint (ideally the vendor API) and capture its fingerprint. Without a baseline there is nothing to compare against.

identityRun.title: 3 · Run the check
identityRun.content: Verification costs a handful of tokens: it inspects protocol fields and counts how the tokenizer splits fixed probe texts.

identityEvidence.title: 4 · Read the evidence
identityEvidence.content: Each probe reports baseline vs observed. The verdict is driven by hard gates — one fatal signal outranks any weighted score.

identity.title: Model identity verification
identity.subtitle: Fingerprint an endpoint and compare it with a baseline you trust, to catch substituted, downgraded or replayed models.

empty.title: No baseline yet — capture one before anything can be verified

setup.title: Setup
setup.baselineHint: A baseline is the fingerprint of an endpoint you trust — ideally the vendor API itself. Verification is always relative to it.

identity.noRun: Run a verification to see the evidence table

modelEcho.name: Model echo
modelEcho.desc: Send a minimal request and compare the `model` field the endpoint reports back.
modelEcho.rationale: Many relays forward the real upstream model name verbatim, leaking the substitution.

invalidModelError.name: Invalid-model error shape
invalidModelError.desc: Request a deliberately non-existent model and record the status code plus error text.
invalidModelError.rationale: Error templates are vendor specific and almost never spoofed by relays.

logprobsSupport.name: logprobs support
logprobsSupport.desc: Ask for `logprobs` and check whether the endpoint honours the field.
logprobsSupport.rationale: A relay that drops fields the real API supports is rewriting the request.

jsonModeSupport.name: JSON mode support
jsonModeSupport.desc: Send `response_format: json_object` and check whether it is accepted.
jsonModeSupport.rationale: Same as logprobs: dropped parameters indicate a proxy in the middle.

cacheReplay.name: Cache replay
cacheReplay.desc: Send the same deterministic request twice and compare the answers and timings.
cacheReplay.rationale: Identical output plus a much faster second call suggests a cached response, not a model.

en.name: Tokenizer · English
en.desc: Count `prompt_tokens` for a fixed English sentence.
en.rationale: Token count is a property of the tokenizer, which is bound to the model family.

zh.name: Tokenizer · Chinese
zh.desc: Count `prompt_tokens` for a fixed Chinese sentence.
zh.rationale: Chinese splits very differently across tokenizers, which makes it highly discriminative.

code.name: Tokenizer · Code
code.desc: Count `prompt_tokens` for a fixed Python snippet.
code.rationale: Whitespace and identifier handling differ sharply between tokenizer families.

emoji.name: Tokenizer · Emoji & rare Unicode
emoji.desc: Count `prompt_tokens` for emoji, ZWJ sequences and rare CJK/math glyphs.
emoji.rationale: Rare codepoints fall back to byte-level splits in a family-specific way.

constantOffset.name: Constant token offset (auto-detected)
constantOffset.desc: When all four fixed-text token counts differ from the baseline by the exact same amount (offset ≥ 2), the engine emits this signal automatically. It usually means a fixed-length system prompt was injected upstream rather than the tokenizer being swapped.
constantOffset.rationale: This is an automatic conclusion from the comparison stage and costs no extra requests. The tokenizer itself still matches the baseline, so this signal is only a caution and does not by itself prove substitution.

common.recordedForBaseline: Recorded for comparison against the baseline. Needs a baseline to judge.

modelEcho.noModel: Endpoint did not return a `model` field, so it cannot confirm what served the request.
modelEcho.pass: Endpoint reports back "{{reported}}", matching the requested model.
modelEcho.warnAlias: Endpoint reports "{{reported}}" for a request made as "{{requested}}" — a version alias is plausible, verify manually.
modelEcho.fail: Endpoint reports "{{reported}}" but the request was made as "{{requested}}".

invalidModelError.recorded: Recorded for comparison against the baseline. Needs a baseline to judge.

logprobsSupport.unsupportedOk: Endpoint accepted the request but omitted logprobs.

cacheReplay.noText: Endpoint returned no text for the cache probe.
cacheReplay.passDistinct: Two identical deterministic requests produced different text, so responses are not replayed verbatim.
cacheReplay.warnSpeedup: Identical output and the second call was {{speedup}}x faster — possible cache replay.
cacheReplay.passIdentical: Identical output at comparable latency, which is expected for temperature 0.

skip.notCompatible: Not applicable to the "{{format}}" protocol — these probes inspect OpenAI-compatible response fields.

compare.baselineMissing: The baseline does not contain this probe — capture a new baseline to enable it.
compare.tokenizerWarn: Off by {{diff}} token(s) from the baseline ({{expected}}). Likely billing granularity.
compare.tokenizerFail: Counted {{observed}} tokens where the baseline has {{expected}} — a different tokenizer.
compare.mismatch: Baseline recorded "{{expected}}" but this endpoint reports "{{observed}}".
compare.constantOffsetOverride: Counted {{observed}} tokens where the baseline has {{baseline}}. Every probe is offset by the same {{offset}} token(s), so the tokenizer itself still matches.
compare.constantOffsetSummary: Every probe is offset by exactly {{offset}} token(s). That is the signature of a fixed-length system prompt being injected upstream — it does not prove substitution by itself.
